Both parts of your direction are done or in motion:

«redacted:editorial»

**The GPU migration is underway** for this device. The agent is upgrading the inference stack to get DirectML support, targeting your RTX 3060 with fp16 weights (with the precision folded into the model fingerprint so GPU and CPU vectors can never silently mix — a clean `reindex --full` is the designed switch), automatic CPU fallback, plus the two hardening items from the performance note: bounded runtime memory and a real no-progress watchdog inside reindex itself.

Its definition of done is deliberately unfakeable: a timed `reindex --full` on this repo with logs proving the DirectML provider actually engaged (silent CPU fallback reporting fake wins is the classic trap — I told it to stop and report rather than paper over), then an end-to-end `ask "what was the most recent change and why was it made"` — the exact question that started today's chain — which should now return a real, cited answer thanks to the recency floor. I'll verify the benchmark myself before committing, as always.
The GPU agent paused itself waiting on its test suite (correctly refusing to run the benchmark concurrently — the RAM rule). Resuming it to finish the job:

The GPU agent is resumed and heading into the payoff phase. From what's visible in its working tree so far, the migration is substantive and thorough: the new device-resolution logic (`resolveTransformersDevice`) and precision-aware `modelFingerprint` are wired all the way through to `doctor` — which will now report the device posture and fingerprint honestly — and it's updated the architecture docs' embedding sections to match.

What's left is the part that can't be faked: the timed `reindex --full` on this repo with logs proving DirectML actually engaged on your 3060 (I've explicitly told it that silent CPU fallback masquerading as a win is the failure mode to watch for), the incremental follow-up run, and then the full-circle moment — asking *"what was the most recent change and why was it made"* with live synthesis, the exact question that kicked off this entire performance investigation. If everything holds, that question goes from "the sources don't contain this information" on a stale, crashing index to a cited answer in seconds on a fresh, GPU-built one.

I'll independently verify the numbers and the suites when it reports, then commit the whole Tier 0 fix.

The agent had parked itself waiting for a notification that was never going to arrive (its background suite had already ended), so I've resumed it with explicit instructions to run everything synchronously this time — verify the test outcome directly, then execute the full benchmark sequence in its own turn: the timed GPU `reindex --full` with proof DirectML engaged, the incremental follow-up, and the live `ask`. No more handing off to background notifications.

Next update you get from me will be the verified benchmark numbers — GPU versus the 30-minutes-and-crashing CPU baseline — and the answer to the question that started all this.
The full report is in with proven numbers. Independent verification — suites first, then a targeted read of the two riskiest bits (no-silent-fallback and legacy-fingerprint compatibility):

attributes.command: cd C:/src/git-for-ai && pnpm turbo build 2>&1 | grep "Tasks:" && cd packages/core && pnpm vitest run 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests " && cd ../cli && pnpm vitest run 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests "

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && grep -n "never a silent\|GIT_FOR_AI_DEVICE=cpu\|legacy" packages/core/src/embeddings/transformersEmbedder.ts | head -6 && grep -n -A6 "export function modelFingerprint" packages/core/src/embeddings/types.ts && node packages/cli/dist/bin.js reindex 2>&1 | tail -3 && node packages/cli/dist/bin.js doctor 2>&1 | grep -E "^  (index|embedder)"
cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git status --short | grep -v "relink.ts" | head -20

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git add architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md architecture/CLI_REFERENCE.md architecture/DATA_MODEL.md packages/cli/src/commands/doctor.test.ts packages/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts packages/cli/src/commands/queryDeps.ts packages/cli/src/commands/reindex.test.ts packages/cli/src/commands/reindex.ts packages/core/package.json packages/core/src/embeddings packages/core/src/index.ts pnpm-lock.yaml && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
GPU embeddings: DirectML on the local GPU - reindex 30min -> 78s

The owner-chosen Tier 0 path, delivered and benchmarked on the real
machine (RTX 3060, 12GB).

- Migrate @xenova/transformers v2 -> @huggingface/transformers 3.8.1
  (onnxruntime-node 1.21 with the DirectML execution provider); the
  durable per-user model cache carries over unchanged.
- Device/precision resolution (resolveTransformersDevice): auto =
  DirectML + fp16 on win32, CPU + int8 elsewhere; overrides via
  GIT_FOR_AI_DEVICE / GIT_FOR_AI_DTYPE and embedder options. A GPU
  load failure is a HARD error naming the escape hatch - never a
  silent CPU fallback, which would mix precisions undetected.
- Precision folds into the model fingerprint (jina-v2-code/768/fp16);
  q8/absent maps to the legacy bare form so existing CPU indexes and
  caches stay valid. Store + state.json + doctor + queryDeps all
  speak the suffixed form; IndexFingerprintError + reindex --full is
  the verified migration path.
- Hardening: ORT session recreated every 512 chunks (under the ~700-
  chunk OOM point); a no-progress watchdog inside runReindex (15min
  default, env-tunable) for live-but-stuck inference; token-aware
  batch packing on DML - two real GPU-only crashes (DirectML 2^32
  tensor-element cap, VRAM OOM on ~5700-token batches) were found
  live and fixed by packing batches to rows*maxTokens^2 <= 40e6.

Benchmark (run alone, DML engagement proven via ORT session logs +
nvidia-smi 100% GPU bursts): cold full reindex of this repo (1,376
chunks) 78.4s vs the ~30-minutes-and-native-OOM CPU baseline (~23x,
and it completes); incremental follow-up 3.6s; live ask "what was the
most recent change and why was it made" returned the actual HEAD
commit with citation - the recency floor and GPU query embedding
working end to end.

Tests: core 257 + cli 213, independently re-verified; device
resolution, fingerprint folding, and precision-mismatch recovery all
covered with fakes (real model never loaded in tests). Docs updated
(ARCHITECTURE 11.3, DATA_MODEL 5.1, CLI_REFERENCE reindex).

Flagged follow-up from the agent: bin.ts's beforeExit guard prints
its OOM hint on ANY nonzero exit (misleading next to a clean typed
error); VRAM peaked at 11.87/12GB on pathological long-token batches
- escape hatches documented.

Implemented by a background Fable 5 agent; independently re-verified
(build, both suites, live incremental reindex + doctor showing the
fp16 fingerprint current) and committed by the orchestrating session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
